Advanced topics in thread safety

A data race happens when two threads access the same memory location at the same time and at least one of them writes.

Locks protect shared data by allowing only one thread at a time to enter the critical section of the program.

Immutable objects are naturally thread safe because their state can never change after they have been created.

Atomic operations are performed as a single indivisible step, so other threads can never observe a half finished update.

Note that the volatile keyword does not make compound operations atomic, which is a common source of subtle bugs.
